messages:
Maya Patel: quick check — post-launch triage: we surfaced ~18 small bugs and 5 customer enhancement asks. do we run a short bug-only sprint or mix bugs+features?
Samir Rao: vote: 1 week bug sprint, then 1 week focused enhancements. separates stability from scope creep.
Elaine Chen: can we rank the bugs by user-impact? some are noisy but not user-facing.
Maya Patel: quick breakdown: 3 are p1 user blockers (signup flake, billing retry, streaming timeout), ~10 low-ux, rest infra/observability. features: embeddings export, larger context, model pinning.
Jordan Lee: ops perspective — bug-only sprint lowers release risk and reduces on-call churn. also faster rollbacks if needed.
Samir Rao: for embeddings export, can we behind-flag and A/B test in parallel to bug sprint? low-risk way to move.
Elaine Chen: i'll draft a 2x2 prioritization (impact x effort) and tag owners. recommend we treat feature asks as backlog candidates unless they clear threshold.
Maya Patel: proposed cadence: Week 1 = bug sprint with a hotfix lane for any regression tied to customers; Week 2 = enhancement sprint working on top 2 features (one quick-ship, one invest). gate features on perf/regressions.
Jordan Lee: note: reserve a small infra window for a hotfix deployment during Week 2 in case of fallout. also keep 20% capacity for on-call.
Samir Rao: add rollout criteria: no p0s outstanding, p99s within baseline +10%, and automated smoke for key flows. also ensure cost per token doesn't regress for model changes.
Maya Patel: action items: Elaine -> prioritization matrix + owner tags by EOD; Samir -> scope minimal impl and flag for embeddings export; Jordan -> reserve infra slots and update runbook; I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow 10am PT to lock sprint.
ProductBot: meeting created: "Post-launch mini-sprint sync" tomorrow 10:00 AM PT.
Maya Patel: thanks all — prefer short updates in this thread, we'll use the meeting to finalize :thumbsup:
